source_text: Illud vero de alio libro meo, quod ad Marcellinum scribens dixi: "Filios mulieris quae serpenti credidit ut libidine corrumperetur, non liberari nisi per Filium Virginis, quae angelo credidit ut sine libidine fetaretur" [n175] ; ita posuisti atque ita voluisti accipi, tamquam dixerim: "Quod Evae serpens commixtus fuerit concubitu corporali"
pass_a_gloss: But that from another book of mine, which writing to Marcellinus I said: 'The sons of the woman who believed the serpent so that she was corrupted by lust are not freed except through the Son of the Virgin, who believed the angel so that she became pregnant without lust'; so you placed and so you wished it to be taken, as if I had said: 'That the serpent was mingled with Eve in bodily lying-together'.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “What I said in another book of mine, writing to Marcellinus, was ‘that the children of the woman who believed the serpent so as to be corrupted by lust are not set free except through the Son of the Virgin, who believed the angel so as to conceive without lust.’ You set it out in such a way, and wanted it taken in such a way, as though I had said ‘that the serpent had joined with Eve in bodily intercourse.’”

choices.why: Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
